analysis:
No concrete security regression found in the supplied files.

Changed behavior:
- coordinator/internal/inference/routeplan/cache_planning.go: planning now derives a preload identity (p.cachePreloadIdentity) instead of Preloader.ReadyFor(PromptContractID). It calls Registry.CachePlanRejection, then NoteDemand(identity) only when not rejected and CachePreloadDemandWithinDeadline holds. It reads PlanningState(identity) and calls commitCachePlanning. Cache scope is still derived from authenticated Account, model and PromptContractID (T-041, A-001).
- The FirstTokenWriteContext wrapper was removed from this function. The first-content deadline bound on optional planning must now be enforced inside commitCachePlanning or CachePreloadDemandWithinDeadline. Neither is in the supplied source. The next pass should confirm they bound registry planning against the receipt-time budget, and that the demand-note path is not a consumer-triggerable preload amplifier.
- cache_planning.go line 46 still gates only on p.Preloader == nil, while the new PreloadPlanning field is optional. An integration pass should confirm the wrapper cannot bypass the Preloader readiness gate.
- cache_preload_selection.go (new): Owner.cachePreloadSelection returns Registry.CachePreloadIdentities(verified) as the admissible set. When refreshAvailability is set, it also returns the verified model IDs that appear in Registry.ListModels(). This is an admission filter keyed on registry models, not on caller input.
- prompt_artifacts.go lines 20-28: SetPromptPreloadController installs the selection source. If SetSelectionSource returns false, it sets promptPreloader=nil, which fails closed.

Not visible: PreloadPlanning, cachePreloadIdentity, commitCachePlanning and PreloadController.SetSelectionSource. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

CHANGELOG.md is documentation only. It describes an SSD cache ceiling of 100 GiB capped at half the available disk, which differs from the threat model's "no fixed ceiling" wording in T-041. It also describes default-on SSD storage of complete Qwen prefix checkpoints, including recurrent state, and a network-prefix-cache allowlist. T-041 may need an update for the new checkpoint at-rest content if those provider changes land in this PR. No provider source was supplied here.
